finding.title: Two checkouts can both reserve the last unit
finding.explanation: reserveStock now reads the row, checks availability in application code, and writes back an absolute `reserved` value. Two checkouts for the last unit can read the same row, both pass the `available < qty` check, and both write `item.reserved + qty`. The second write overwrites the first, so two reservations hold one unit and `reserved` undercounts. The removed reserve_stock() SQL function did the check and the increment under a row lock.
finding.reasoningSummary: The diff deletes the only call to reserve_stock(). git_history shows it was added in #977 to fix overselling on limited drops. The new code runs outside db.$transaction, and an update with a computed literal is not a compare-and-set.

evidence.text: Carts A and B check out TEE-BLK-M (onHand 10, reserved 9) 4 ms apart. Both read reserved = 9 and see 1 available. Both write reserved = 10. Two reservations now exist for one unit.
git log -S reserve_stock: added in #977 "Fix oversell on limited drops" (row lock inside the SQL function)
